case_title: G. Ramesh v. Kanike Harish Kumar Ujwal & Anr.
accused_occupation: Employed with the National Bank of Kuwait (stated in the first respondent's defence; not a court finding)
accused_victim_relationship: Relative (the second accused is the son of the complainant's brother-in-law)
statutory_provisions: NI Act s.138 (cheque dishonour), read with s.141 (offences by companies, including firms); CrPC s.482 (quashing petition)
evidence_type: Documentary (dishonoured cheques and averments in the complaint); no trial evidence discussed
trial_court_outcome: Not stated (no verdict; proceedings before the Special Judicial Magistrate pending; NBWs issued and later recalled)
high_court_outcome: Section 482 petition allowed; proceedings on the Section 138 complaint quashed
neutral_facts: The accused firm carried on data-entry work, taking contracts and sub-contracting them. In August 2010 the victim was given a sub-contract on payment of a caution deposit of Rs 1,00,000, made through two cheques credited to the firm's account on 30 August 2010. The victim performed data-entry work from September to December 2010, valued at Rs 8,50,000. For that work the accused issued two cheques: dated 1 November 2010 for Rs 2,00,000 and 18 December 2010 for Rs 2,50,000. When the victim presented them through the victim's bank, both were returned unpaid for insufficient funds, and the victim requested payment of the dishonoured amounts with later months' dues. In February 2011 one accused transferred Rs 1,00,000 into the victim's account and promised to pay the balance. Later, a managing partner issued two further cheques, dated 30 May 2011 and 19 July 2011, each for Rs 2,00,000. The first was returned unpaid on 30 May 2011. After the accused assured the victim that both would be honoured on re-presentation in July 2011, the victim presented them; both were returned unpaid on 14 July and 20 July 2011 for insufficient funds. The victim alleges the accused then avoided contact. A notice of demand was issued on 1 August 2011, and no payment followed.
number_of_offences: 1 charged (NI Act s.138, read with s.141); 0 finally upheld
financial_property_loss: Cheques of Rs 2,00,000 and Rs 2,50,000 (first set) and Rs 2,00,000 each (second set) returned unpaid; balance of Rs 7,50,000 and caution deposit of Rs 1,00,000 alleged unpaid
key_evidence_accepted: Averments in the complaint: first set of cheques returned for insufficiency of funds, Rs 1,00,000 transfer on 8 and 10 February 2011, and assurance that second set would be honoured in July 2011
witness_credibility: Not stated (no witness assessment; the Court read the complaint averments as a whole)
post_offence_conduct: Alleged by the complainant that the accused avoided contact after the dishonour; the Court made no finding
trial_duration: offence: not given; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 13 June 2018; Supreme Court: 05 April 2019
legal_representation: Appellant (complainant): Ms. Bhabhna Das, Krishna Dev Jagarlamudi. Respondents: Abhimanyu Bhandari, Ms. Akriti Chaubey, Ms. Roohina Dua, Kunwar Aditya Singh, Ejaz Maqbool, S. Udaya Kumar Sagar, Mrityunjai Singh. State: Not stated
investigation_status: Private complaint under s.138 NI Act instituted 19 September 2011; no police investigation discussed; trial stage pending
procedural_irregularity: None noted as a procedural lapse (the Court noted the High Court overlooked that the first accused is a partnership firm)
appeal_history: Trial court: proceedings pending, NBWs recalled. High Court: s.482 petition allowed, proceedings quashed. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, High Court order set aside
prosecution_argument: The High Court erred in quashing the complaint; the averments are sufficient to meet the requirement of s.141 NI Act
defence_argument: No averment that the first respondent was in charge of and responsible for the business; he lives in Kuwait and has no day-to-day connection with the firm; the High Court's quashing should not be disturbed under Article 136
legal_principle_applied: Under s.141(1) NI Act, a firm is included in 'company'; the sufficiency of averments is judged on a holistic reading of the complaint, applying the Gunmala Sales test
precedent_relied_upon: Gunmala Sales Private Limited v. Anu Mehta and Others (2015) 1 SCC 103
other_sentence_order: Liberty given to the first respondent to apply before the Trial Judge for exemption from appearing at trial, to be considered in accordance with law

case_title.quote: G. RAMESH v. KANIKE HARISH KUMAR UJWAL & ANR. (Criminal Appeal No. 603 of 2019)

number_of_accused.quote: The High Court was in error in quashing the criminal case against the first respondent.

accused_gender.quote: The defence of the first respondent is that, he resides in Kuwait where he is employed with the National Bank of Kuwait.

accused_occupation.quote: he resides in Kuwait where he is employed with the National Bank of Kuwait. Hence, he has no day to day connection with the affairs of the partnership firm.

victim_gender.quote: the complainant could not continue said work from the month of January 2011, as he had no money to pay the salaries of his employees.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: As the accused no. 2 is son of brother in law of complainant, he believed them and kept quite for some time.

statutory_provisions.quote: a complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881

evidence_type.quote: The complaint contains a recital of the fact that the first set of cheques were returned for insufficiency of funds.

trial_court_outcome.quote: Non-bailable warrants were issued against the first respondent as he failed to appear in the proceedings. The warrants were recalled.

high_court_outcome.quote: While allowing a petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 instituted by the first respondent, the High Court quashed the proceedings

final_outcome.quote: We accordingly allow the appeal and set aside the impugned judgment and order of the High Court dated 13 June 2018.

neutral_facts.quote: The accused are alleged to have obtained a caution deposit of Rs 1,00,000 and to have assigned the job of data entry to the complainant.

attempt_completion.quote: the cheques were returned unpaid due to insufficient funds in their bank account

number_of_offences.quote: a complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881

financial_property_loss.quote: The complainant did the data entry work for said four months worth of Rs 8,50,000 as per rates of understanding.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: The averments are sufficient to meet the requirement of Section 141(1).

witness_credibility.quote: This is a matter which has to be determined on a holistic reading of the complaint.

trial_duration.quote: We accordingly allow the appeal and set aside the impugned judgment and order of the High Court dated 13 June 2018.

legal_representation.quote: Ms. Bhabhna Das, Krishna Dev Jagarlamudi, Advocates for the Appellant. Abhimanyu Bhandari, Ms. Akriti Chaubey, Ms. Roohina Dua, Kunwar Aditya Singh, Ejaz Maqbool, S. Udaya Kumar Sagar, Mrityunjai Singh, Advs. for the Respondents.

investigation_status.quote: The complaint was instituted on 19 September 2011 before the Special Judicial Magistrate First Class, Mahabubnagar.

procedural_irregularity.quote: The fact that the first accused, in the present case, is a partnership firm of which the remaining two accused are partners has been missed by the High Court.

appeal_history.quote: We accordingly allow the appeal and set aside the impugned judgment and order of the High Court dated 13 June 2018.

prosecution_argument.quote: the High Court was manifestly in error in quashing the complaint. Besides relying on the decision of this Court in Gunmala Sales Private Limited

defence_argument.quote: there was no averment in the complaint that the first respondent was incharge of and was responsible to the "company" for the conduct of the business.

legal_principle_applied.quote: a partnership is a compendious expression to denote the partners who comprise of the firm. By the deeming fiction in Explanation (a) the expression company is defined to include a firm.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Gunmala Sales Private Limited v. Anu Mehta and Others 5 , learned counsel submitted

other_sentence_order.quote: We leave it open to the first respondent to move an application in that regard before the learned Trial Judge which would be considered in accordance with law.
